issues.description: The Meal constructor parameter order in the template does not match the specification and the solution. The problem statement (UML) and the solution expect Meal(String name, String[] ingredients), but the template declares Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This will cause compile-time confusion and prevent students from using the provided Main examples and following the specified API.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Meal constructor in the template to have the signature public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) to match the UML in the problem statement and the solution. Update the parameter order accordingly so the provided Main examples compile and students can implement expected behavior.

issues.description: The Problem Statement (UML) and the Solution expect the Meal constructor signature to be Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) (name first, ingredients second). However, the Template repository defines the Meal constructor with the parameters reversed: Meal(String[] ingredients, String name). This mismatch between the template and the problem/solution creates a direct mapping and compilation confusion for students (the sample usages in Main and the UML assume the name-first signature).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the Template Meal.java to match the problem UML and the Solution: declare as public Meal(String name, String[] ingredients) and assign fields accordingly (this aligns constructor signature with Main usage and the UML).
